title: Flowering soil container: chlorosis and marginal necrosis

context.pH: reported high; numerical value and method not supplied

observed: Widespread fan-leaf yellowing in the supplied photo
Brown leaf margins and necrotic tips
Visible flowering structures; photo alone does not establish progression

hypotheses.name: Excess soluble salts / root-zone osmotic stress
supports: Frequent heavy fertilizer input in limited media volume
Tip and margin necrosis compatible with salinity injury
confirm: Representative repeatable soil-extract EC elevated relative to crop-system reference and prior baseline
Documented high feed input with salt accumulation over time
challenge: Representative same-method EC not elevated and no accumulation trend

hypotheses.name: High-pH-associated nutrient availability limitation
confirm: Calibrated numeric soil pH measured with documented sampling method
Corroborating soil or tissue nutrient analysis
challenge: Appropriate repeatable pH and no corresponding availability imbalance

hypotheses.name: Excess moisture / low root-zone aeration
supports: Every-other-day irrigation could limit dryback in some soils
confirm: Persistently saturated media, poor drainage, or impaired roots
challenge: Normal moisture cycling and well-aerated healthy roots

hypotheses.name: Specific elemental shortage (e.g., K or Mg)
supports: Some leaf symptoms resemble deficiency patterns
confirm: Tissue/nutrient-input evidence plus age-dependent symptom progression
challenge: Elemental supply adequate; another measured stress explains the pattern

evidenceToCollect: Calibrated soil pH, sampling method, date and location
EC (mS/cm), sample extraction method, repeat trend and calibration
Fertilizer composition and actual input EC with volumes
Container moisture, drainage and root assessment
Date-stamped comparable leaf photographs and first-affected leaf age
decisionRules: Do not call nutrient lockout confirmed from one photo, runoff sample or pH value
Do not compare EC values from different sampling methods as a direct trend
Avoid changing multiple variables simultaneously before establishing a baseline
Old necrotic tissue does not recover; new damage and progression are follow-up indicators
Improvement after correction supports but does not uniquely prove a proposed mechanism
workingConclusion: Fertilizer-associated salinity and pH-related stress are leading competing or coexisting explanations. Root-zone measurements are required to resolve them.

sources.scope: Deficiency symptomology in controlled cannabis hydroponics; does not validate a soil-specific diagnosis from imagery
Cannabis nutrient-concentration research; does not establish this container's EC
